title: Lesson 10: Addressing Fear and Skepticism as a Leader
description: Addressing fear and skepticism as a leader: the difference between fear and skepticism as two distinct reactions, why arguing either one away backfires, the six-step framework for addressing the concern underneath, and how to run a working session that turns a skeptic into an engaged tester.

questions.question: A team member doubts the tool works and asks for evidence that it saves time. Which reaction is this?
options: Fear, which calls for reassurance that nobody in the team will lose their role
Skepticism, which calls for specific evidence of what the tool does
Fear, which calls for letting the person set the adoption pace
Skepticism, which calls for restating the rollout plan more firmly
questions.explanation: Skepticism is a rational doubt, and it answers to evidence, provided the evidence is specific and honest. Reassurance aimed at feelings does not resolve a question about whether the tool actually works.

questions.question: An employee says the tool will take their job, and the leader answers with productivity figures. Why does that response usually fail?
options: The figures are usually inaccurate and easy for anyone in the room to disprove
The employee hears the worry was not understood and goes quiet instead
The employee has not been trained to read productivity figures
The employee needs the figures in writing before accepting them
questions.explanation: Arguing against a fear signals that the concern was never taken seriously, and the silence that follows is not agreement. The worry goes underground, where it keeps eroding the program without being addressable.

questions.question: A leader has named the concern and shown which tasks change. What does handing the team control over the pace add?
options: It shifts responsibility for the results onto the team itself
It removes the need for any further communication from the leadership team
It lowers fear by letting people shape how the tool enters their work
It guarantees that adoption will finish on the planned schedule
questions.explanation: Fear spikes when change is imposed and drops when people have a say. A team that can shape how the tool arrives stops treating it as an outside threat.
